description:
FOUND + FIXED s517b (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-16) -- PRE-EXISTING on main dc87c403, exposed by the zlib shim (#3161): once Compress::Zlib loads, Archive::Tar reads every archive through IO::Zlib, and the everyday program modules/Archive-Tar-Compress (identical to perl on main because Archive::Tar fell back to plain IO) died "Can't use string (...) as a SCALAR ref".

REPRO (perl 5.40.3):
  sub fill { my $r = shift; $$r .= "a" x 150 for 1 .. 3 } my $ob = ""; fill(\$ob); my $y = "Y"; $ob = \$y; print ref($ob)   # perl SCALAR; main "" (and length 1)
  same with $z = {k=>1}: perl HASH, main "".

CAUSE: box-set's magic-cell branch hands the setter (unbox value) for any unblessed box value -- right for a real lvalue magic (substr, pos, vec), wrong for the :strbuf cell, which is REPRESENTATION (the setter resets and box-sets the unboxed target).

FIX: box-set treats a :strbuf cell as replaceable: it drops the cell and takes the ordinary store path with the original value.  Guard Pl/t/zlib-01.t "strbuf store and lvalue args" (fails on main).  Everyday modules/Archive-Tar-Compress identical again.

=== DONE (s517b) ===
subject: Assigning a REFERENCE to a scalar whose box holds a long `.=` buffer (:strbuf cell, #2115) stored the ref's TARGET through the cell setter -- the ref was lost; IO::Uncompress::Base::read's `$out_buffer = \*$self->{Pending}` made every IO::Zlib read die
